title: End-to-End Neural Modeling of EM Response and Design Performance for Free-Form RFIC Passives
claim: Exact downstream solvers collapse under tiny input perturbations, while a learned solver stays stable and accurate under imperfect inputs.
layout: 1 panel, line plot with a legend overlaid inside the axes
description: A single scatter-and-line plot. The x-axis is R²_EM, the accuracy of the input EM response, running from 0.96 to 1.00. The y-axis is R²_design, the downstream design performance, running from 0.7 to 1.0. A teal line with circular markers for the Learned Neural Solver sits near 0.97–0.98 across the whole range and rises slowly toward the right. A dashed mauve line with square markers for the Valid GT Solver (R² > 0) appears only at the far right edge near x=1.0. It drops sharply from about 1.0 to 0.85. A row of olive triangles for the Failed GT Solver (R² ≤ 0) is clamped along the bottom at 0.7 across almost all x values. The legend is inside the plot area. The light-gray background and dashed grid make the plot clean. The eye goes first to the flat teal line and then to the triangles below it.
caption: Solver stability under imperfect EM response. The ground-truth (GT) solver achieves $R^2=1$ with noiseless input, but its design-performance $R^2$ becomes negative even at $R^2_{\mathrm{EM}}\approx 0.9984$. In contrast, the learned neural solver remains stable given imperfect EM responses. [ref] details the evaluation protocol and illustrates the magnitude of the perturbations.
abstract: Passive matching networks are critical components in radio-frequency integrated circuits (RFICs), but their design is bottlenecked by expensive finite-difference-based electromagnetic (EM) simulation. We propose an end-to-end neural framework for free-form RFIC passives that predicts both EM response and downstream design performance under varying frequency and circuit contexts, combining a frequency-conditioned neural simulator with a circuit-conditioned neural solver. To improve design performance prediction, the simulator outputs a neural EM response consisting of both the explicit EM response and a complementary response, together with a dependence regularizer that encourages the two responses to capture orthogonal information. To evaluate the proposed framework, we construct a large-scale dataset of free-form passive layouts, synthesized from both expert-designed contours and random paths. Our 21M-parameter model achieves high accuracy across a broad frequency range, circuit contexts and passive matching settings, with $R^2>0.98$ for almost all targets, while providing orders-of-magnitude faster evaluation than traditional EM simulation. Code available at https://github.com/ETH-IDEAS/RFIC-NeuralSim.
